How to do itFront Squat

Torso angle

Right
CHEST TALL
Wrong
CHEST FALLS

Right: Chest tall, elbows high at the bottom.

Wrong: Chest falling forward, elbows dropping.

Keep your elbows up so your shoulders hold the bar.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows dropThe elbows drop and the bar starts to slip.
  2. Chest falls forwardThe chest falls and the torso tips forward.
LowerControlled
Drive up 
Look closer

Grip

Your shoulders hold the bar, hands loose round it, elbows high. Or cross your arms over it, elbows high.

Common handling mistakes

  • Chest falling, elbows dropping

    Fix: Elbows up, chest tall.

  • Hands holding the bar up

    Fix: Let your shoulders carry the bar. Try a fingertip rack.

  • Bailing with no safeties set

    Fix: Set the safeties. To bail, drop the bar forward and step back.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this mostly in the front of your thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe hands are holding the bar up.

    FixPush your shoulders forward and up. Try a fingertip rack.

  • Usually meansThe torso is tipping forward.

    FixKeep the elbows high and the chest tall.

  • Usually meansThe bar is too far back or the shoulders are not up.

    FixRaise your shoulders slightly so the bar only touches lightly.

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the safety bars just below your lowest squat depth.

  2. 2

    Bar between throat and shoulders. Shoulders pushed forward and slightly up.

  3. 3

    Loose full grip, elbows high.

  4. 4

    Heels hip width or a little wider, toes out 15-30 degrees.

  5. 5

    Walk out one step back on each leg. Brace hard each rep.

Risks and when to stop

  • A failed rep with no safeties set.
  • Holding your breath under heavy load raises blood pressure.
  • Bar pressing on the throat.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

Back pain

Pain, numbness, tingling or weakness in both legs? Numb genitals or anus? Bladder, bowel or sexual changes? Chest pain? Serious accident? Get emergency help now. Sudden severe or fast-worsening pain? Hot, cold, shivery or unwell? See a doctor today.

No better in a few weeks? See a doctor.

How to do itBodyweight Squat

Bottom position

Right
HEELS DOWN
Wrong
HEELS LIFT

Right: Shin and torso parallel, back flat, heels down.

Wrong: Heels lifted at the bottom.

Start by moving your hips back, then down.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Heels liftThe heels come off the floor at the bottom.
  2. Weight on toesThe weight rolls forward onto the toes.
Lower 
Drive up 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your thighs and buttocks.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe torso is rounding at the bottom.

    FixStop higher, where the back is still flat.

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Feet slightly wider than hip width, toes slightly out.

  2. 2

    Shoulders down and back, brace, chest up.

  3. 3

    Hips back, then down, back flat. Shins forward under control.

  4. 4

    Lower to thighs about parallel. Knees may pass the toes slightly.

  5. 5

    Breathe out, push the feet down, hips and chest rise together.

Risks and when to stop

  • Knees held behind the toes likely load the hips and lower back.

How to do itWall Sit

Knee over ankle

Right
SHIN VERTICAL
Wrong
KNEE PAST TOES

Right: Shin vertical, knee directly above the ankle.

Wrong: Feet close to the wall, knee past the toes.

Back on wall

Right
ON THE WALL
Wrong
OFF THE WALL

Right: Back and buttocks flat on the wall.

Wrong: Buttocks away from the wall.

Keep your back and buttocks on the wall.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Feet too closeThe feet sit too close to the wall.
  2. Knees past toesThe knees push forward past the toes.
Hold30-60 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansFeet too close to the wall, or the hold is too deep.

    FixWalk your feet further out. Hold higher on the wall.

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the hold.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Back on the wall, feet out front, shoulder width, toes slightly out.

  2. 2

    Slide down until hips and knees are about 90 degrees.

  3. 3

    Knees right above the ankles. Move the feet if not.

  4. 4

    Knees over the second toe, ankles not rolling.

  5. 5

    Hold 30-60 seconds and keep breathing steadily.

Risks and when to stop

  • Blood pressure rises during the hold, more the deeper you go.
  • Holding the breath raises blood pressure further during the hold.
  • Feet too close to the wall load the kneecap more.

How to do itPistol Squat

Standing foot

Right
HEEL DOWN
Wrong
HEEL LIFTS

Right: Standing foot flat at the bottom.

Wrong: Heel lifted.

Reach your arms forward for balance.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Heel liftsThe standing heel comes off the floor at the bottom.
  2. Knee forwardThe knee drives forward as the weight rolls onto the toes.
LowerSlow
Drive upSlow
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your standing thigh.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe deep single-leg bend is too much for now.

    FixBack off and check your form. Use a box, support or easier version.

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Master air squats and single-leg balance first.

  2. 2

    Stand tall, arms forward, and shift onto one leg.

  3. 3

    Lift the other leg forward, knee straight.

  4. 4

    Brace, then send the hips back and bend the knee.

  5. 5

    Go as low as mobility allows, foot flat. Press up, no bounce.

Risks and when to stop

  • High knee demand in the deep single-leg bend.
  • Advanced skill: attempting it before the basics.

How to do itJump Squat

Landing

Right
KNEES BENT
Wrong
LOCKED KNEES

Right: Mid-foot landing, hips back and down, knees bent.

Wrong: Straight, locked knees on landing.

Take-off

Right
HIPS STRAIGHT
Wrong
HIPS BENT

Right: Ankles, knees and hips fully extended together.

Wrong: Jumping with the hips still bent.

Send the hips back, then down, keeping the back flat.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Knees straightThe knees stay straight and locked on the landing.
  2. Hips highThe hips stay high instead of dropping back and down.
LowerControlled
JumpExplosive
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your thighs and buttocks.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansFault: locked knees or knees shooting far forward on landing.

    FixLand softly, hips back. Make the jumps smaller.

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop jumping.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Learn to squat and land first. Start with small jumps.

  2. 2

    Feet hip width, hands loosely at the chest, brace.

  3. 3

    Hips back, then down, until the heels are about to lift.

  4. 4

    Brief pause, then jump: ankles, knees and hips extend together.

  5. 5

    Land quietly on the mid-foot, rolling to the heels, hips back.

Risks and when to stop

  • Locked-knee landings may lead to knee injuries.
  • Knees travelling far forward on landing add knee stress.
  • Knees caving inward on landing.

How to do itStep-Up

Trunk angle

Right
TORSO UPRIGHT
Wrong
TRUNK FORWARD

Right: Torso upright as the top leg drives.

Wrong: Trunk thrown forward to get up.

Lead foot

Right
WHOLE FOOT DOWN
Wrong
FRONT OF FOOT

Right: Whole foot flat on the box.

Wrong: Only the front of the foot on the box.

Put your whole lead foot firmly on the box.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Trunk thrown forwardThe trunk lurches forward to get up.
  2. Back foot pushesThe bottom foot pushes off to help.
Rise 
LowerControlled
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the top leg's thigh and glute.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansFault: the bottom foot pushing you up.

    FixLet the top leg do the work.

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Dumbbells at the sides, palms facing in, feet hip width apart.

  2. 2

    Whole foot firmly on the box, knee over the second toe.

  3. 3

    Stand up with the top leg, little help from the bottom foot.

  4. 4

    Step the trailing foot down first, controlling the way down.

  5. 5

    Repeat on the same leg or alternate.

Risks and when to stop

  • Dropping off the box instead of lowering under control.
  • Knee or ankle collapsing inward.

How to do itForward Lunge

Front shin

Right
SHIN VERTICAL
Wrong
KNEE FORWARD

Right: Hips dropped, front shin about vertical.

Wrong: Hips driven forward, front shin tipped far forward.

Back position

Right
BACK STRAIGHT
Wrong
CHEST FORWARD

Right: Back straight over the hips.

Wrong: Chest pitched forward over the front thigh.

Drop the hips toward the floor rather than driving them forward.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Knee drives forwardThe hips and front knee drive forward, and the shin tips far over the foot.
  2. Shin tips forwardThe front shin tips past vertical, the knee ahead of the toes.
StepSlow
LowerSmooth
Rise 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your thighs and glutes. Longer steps work glutes and hamstrings more, shorter the quads.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe chest is leaning forward.

    FixStay upright. Go lighter if you can't.

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Feet hip width, dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in.

  2. 2

    Step forward heel first, moving the weight onto it slowly.

  3. 3

    Lower slowly, hips straight down, back knee almost to the floor.

  4. 4

    Push through the front foot and step back to the start.

  5. 5

    Alternate legs. Keep the back straight throughout.

Risks and when to stop

  • More kneecap-joint load than the reverse lunge.
  • Too heavy a load costs the upright trunk, the controlled descent and balance.
  • Crashing into the bottom position instead of lowering under control.

How to do itWalking Lunge

Trunk angle

Right
TRUNK UPRIGHT
Wrong
CHEST FORWARD

Right: Trunk upright over the hips at the bottom.

Wrong: Chest pitched forward over the front thigh.

Front shin

Right
SHIN VERTICAL
Wrong
SHIN TIPPED

Right: Hips dropped, front shin about vertical.

Wrong: Hips driven forward, front shin tipped far forward.

At the bottom, keep the front shin about vertical.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Trunk pitches forwardThe trunk pitches forward over the front thigh at the bottom.
  2. Head dropsThe head and chest drop toward the front knee.
LowerControlled
Rise 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your thighs and your glutes.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe chest is leaning forward.

    FixStay upright. Go lighter if you can't.

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Stand with feet about hip width apart, dumbbells at your sides.

  2. 2

    Step forward heel first, weight onto it slowly, no sideways tilt.

  3. 3

    Lower slowly, back knee toward the front heel, until it lightly touches.

  4. 4

    Push through the front foot to stand. Swing the back leg forward.

  5. 5

    Keep alternating legs as you move forward.

Risks and when to stop

  • Too heavy a load costs the upright trunk, the controlled descent and balance.
  • Crashing into the bottom position instead of lowering under control.

Front shin

Right: Hips dropped, front shin leaning only slightly.

Wrong: Hips driven forward, front shin tipped far forward.

  2. Shin tips forwardThe front shin tips past vertical, the knee ahead of the toes.
StepSlow
Lower 
Rise 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your front thigh and glutes.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansA longer step works these more.

    FixShorten the step for more front-thigh work.

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Stand with feet together, shoulders down and back, trunk braced.

  2. 2

    Balance on one foot, step forward, land heel first.

  3. 3

    Move the weight over slowly, upper body level.

  4. 4

    Drop the hips until the front thigh is about parallel.

  5. 5

    Push off firmly with the front leg to stand back up.

Risks and when to stop

  • Losing balance on the step. Learn single-leg standing first.
  • Uncontrolled forward shin travel when the hips drive forward.

Front shin

Right
SHIN VERTICAL
Wrong
KNEE FORWARD

Right: Front shin about vertical.

Wrong: Front knee slid forward, shin tipped far forward.

Trunk angle

Right
TRUNK UPRIGHT
Wrong
CHEST FORWARD

Right: Trunk upright over the hips.

Wrong: Chest pitched forward.

Keep the trunk upright.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Knee slides forwardThe front knee slides forward and the shin tips well past vertical.
  2. Shin tips forwardThe front shin tips past vertical, the knee ahead of the toes.
LowerSmooth
RiseSmooth

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front thigh. The front of the back hip stretches.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Stand in a split stance, one foot forward, one back.

  2. 2

    Bend both knees, lowering smoothly until the back knee lightly touches.

  3. 3

    Keep the trunk upright and the front shin about vertical.

  4. 4

    Stand back up until the front knee is about straight.

Risks and when to stop

  • Crashing into the bottom instead of lowering smoothly.

How to do itBulgarian Split Squat

Rear knee

Right
JUST ABOVE FLOOR
Wrong
KNEE RESTS

Right: Rear knee just above or lightly touching the floor.

Wrong: Rear knee resting on the floor.

Rest the top of the rear foot on a bench about knee height.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Knee restsDropping into the bottom, the rear knee rests on the floor.
LowerControlled
Stand 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front thigh and glute, most at the bottom. The rear hip stretches.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansNot a training feeling.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set a bench or box about knee height behind you.

  2. 2

    Rear foot laces-down on it, front foot about three foot-lengths ahead.

  3. 3

    Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.

  4. 4

    Lower under control until the rear knee lightly touches the floor.

  5. 5

    Do all reps on one leg, then switch.

Risks and when to stop

  • Too heavy a load ends in a crash into the bottom.
  • Front knee drifting inward or outward.
